description:
Somos un equipo de jóvenes guatemaltecos que combina grandes ideas usando la tecnológica de la NASA para transformar algo innovador en la agricultura.

Nuestra misión es llevar los datos satelitales hasta el campo, creando soluciones inteligentes que ayuden a los agricultores a tomar mejores decisiones, cuidar sus cultivos y adaptarse al cambio climático.

Creemos que las grandes soluciones nacen cuando unimos nuestras raíces con la tecnología del futuro.
summary: AGRO-MAYA ESPACIAL is an interactive web platform that helps you identify climate changes in your selected geographic area by integrating space technology and local knowledge (soil type) to support agricultural planning through selecting crops adapted to weather changes and sustainably managing natural resources. It offers techniques for soil exploration, monitoring, and analysis, with a focus on precision and sustainability. The Mayan guide will walk you through the platform’s features so you can get to know it; you can pause it at any time. You’ll be able to create a user account and save your history of PDF reports, which will also be available for you to download to your device
details:
What does it do, and how does it work?

The AGRO-MAYA ESPACIAL platform uses NASA data and is designed with the farmers of the future in mind. Upon launching, the Mayan territorial guide will appear to welcome the user and guide them on their journey through the platform to learn about its features. The user can pause the guide at any time and resume when they need assistance. The user selects any geographic coordinate on the “Territorial Map” to analyze its satellite topography. Based on georeferencing, it also analyzes historical climate data and future projections to help plan resilient crop rotations, generating technical reports and graphs that can be exported as PDFs. The platform saves the reports so the user can access them whenever needed, and they can also download them directly to their device.

What benefits does it offer?

TERRITORIAL MAP

Interactive Satellite Viewer: Explore the territory in real time with satellite layers, SRTM terrain data, and a time simulator.

NASA SRTM and POWER Telemetry: Instant quantitative summary of the selected coordinate or parcel.

Saved Plots and Active Area: Manage your study areas, review climate alerts, and export reports.

CLIMATE ANALYSIS

NASA POWER Climate Charts: Visualize historical temperature trends (1995–2024) and future projections through 2050.

1995–2050 Decadal Matrix: an exact numerical table by year to validate temperature and precipitation projections.

Agroclimatic Conditions Fusion: combines satellite data with empirical calibration to identify planting windows and stress conditions.

SENSORS AND CROP ROTATION

Chemical and Soil Profile: structural fertility radar (N, P, K, pH, organic matter, and CIC) tailored to the soil on your plot.

Adaptive Crop Rotation Plan: a multi-cycle sequence designed by AI to fix nitrogen and withstand droughts.

Crop Rotation and Techniques Explorer: Simulates crop combinations and reviews precision monitoring protocols.

IoT SENSORS

Field IoT Nodes: List of active LoRaWAN sensors and registration of new stations on the plot.

Live Telemetry and Simulator: sensor graph and sudden-change simulator to test automatic alerts.

REPORTS AND AI

Self-Learning AI: the model learns from every real observation you enter and reduces its mean absolute error (MAE).

Adaptive Forecasting and PDF Reports: Generates executive summaries covering 5, 15, or 25 years and archives downloadable reports.

Computer Vision and Plant Pathology Prediction: Analyzes photographs of leaves or plants to identify pests, fungi, and nutrient deficiencies.

What is the expected impact of the project?

The AGRO- MAYA ESPACIAL Project has multidimensional impact because it translates complex aerospace technology into practical tools for farmers.

1. Environmental and Climate Adaptation

By projecting scenarios through the year 2050 using NASA data, farmers can anticipate droughts, heat waves, or changes in rainfall patterns before they occur. Smart crop rotation plans promote natural nitrogen fixation and maintain organic matter balance, reducing erosion and soil degradation. Efficient Use of Resources: By cross-referencing satellite data with real-time IoT sensors, irrigation is optimized, and the unnecessary use of agrochemicals is reduced.

2. Economic and Productive

Loss Reduction: Early detection of pests, fungi, and nutrient deficiencies through computer vision (leaf photos) prevents diseases from spreading and ruining the harvest. Savings on inputs: Knowing the exact chemical profile of the soil (N, P, K, pH) prevents the purchase of fertilizers that the soil does not need. Access to financing: Generating structured technical reports in PDF format supports farmers with scientific evidence, facilitating applications for agricultural loans, parametric insurance, or sustainability certifications.

3. Social and Cultural

Technological democratization: Makes scientific-grade tools (satellite telemetry and artificial intelligence) available to small and medium-sized producers who normally do not have access to expensive agronomic consulting services. Cultural Identity and Ownership: By integrating a Mayan territorial guide with a user-friendly, interactive design, it breaks down the barrier of technological intimidation and connects the territory’s ancestral wisdom with modern space science.

4. Scientific and Educational

Continuous Improvement Through AI: The system functions as a collective learning network. Each real-world observation entered by users trains the model, reducing its mean absolute error (MAE) and creating an increasingly accurate local agroclimatic database. Knowledge Transfer: The guided mode and simulators allow rural youth and new farmers to learn about soil science, climatology, and precision agriculture in a hands-on way. Providing accurate data to farmers.

¿What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

Google AI Studio was used to program the platform.

¿In what way is your project creative?

The AGRO-MAYA ESPACIAL platform includes a Maya territorial guide to help users learn about the platform and use it properly. The design was inspired by the Maya civilization of our country, Guatemala, as they were great astronomers who, without using telescopes, combined observations made with the naked eye with a vigesimal mathematical system to guide agriculture. The name came from combining agriculture (Agro), the Maya civilization (Maya), and astronomy (Espacial).

What factors did your team take into account?

We took into account the objectives of the challenge and the needs of farmers.
